question: Should OpenClaw accept the legacy Installed Apps opt-in reset and ship this Play disclosure/Data Safety rollout after the branch is refreshed and the release-ref ordering bug is fixed?
rationale: The consent gate is privacy-protective, but resetting existing opt-ins and adding release-credential Data Safety automation are compatibility and rollout choices that need maintainer ownership.

options.title: Accept with release-lane fix
options.body: Approve the legacy opt-in reset, fix the release-ref ordering, verify Play Console/Data Safety/privacy materials, refresh the branch, and land the PR.

options.title: Revise disclosure or persistence
options.body: Request changes to wording, placement, consent-version handling, or legacy opt-in behavior before accepting the rollout.

options.title: Hold for Play materials
options.body: Keep the PR open but unmerged until the Data Safety CSV, Play Console state, privacy policy, and review artifacts are ready to ship together.

recommendation.title: Accept with release-lane fix
recommendation.body: Approve the legacy opt-in reset, fix the release-ref ordering, verify Play Console/Data Safety/privacy materials, refresh the branch, and land the PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Android settings and preference history makes this the best available owner for the conflict refresh and legacy opt-in rollout decision.
